topic: Smart India Hackathon (SIH) 2022-2025 winning solutions in software/AI/computer-vision/surveillance/analytics, judging rubric, and recurring patterns judges reward
findings: OFFICIAL RUBRIC (repeated verbatim in AICTE/SIH guidelines and nodal-centre reports, e.g. NorthCap Univ SIH-2024 report, GDSC-BITW guide): ideas/teams are evaluated on 'novelty of the idea, complexity, clarity and details in the prescribed format, feasibility, practicability, sustainability, scale of impact, user experience and potential for future work progression'. The mandatory Idea-PPT template (max 6 slides incl. title, PDF only) forces four sections: Technical Approach (tech stack + flowcharts/prototype), Feasibility & Viability (risks + mitigation), Impact & Benefits (social/economic/environmental), Research & References. Scoring per Scribd 'Evaluation Guideline for SIH 2023': 1-20 per criterion per round, weighted to a final score out of 100. Internal (college) hackathons typically use 5 rubrics x 10 marks = 50: Innovation/Originality, Feasibility/Realistic Implementation, Social-Environmental Impact/Business Value, Technical Execution, Presentation.

GRAND-FINALE ROUND STRUCTURE (36 h, 3 jury evaluations + 2-3 mentoring sessions; 3 jurors per PS who follow the same teams throughout; marks entered into SIH portal). Official SOP language (Swaminarayan Univ nodal-centre report, Dec 2025): Round 1 = 'solution presentation, innovation, feasibility, and execution planning'; Round 2 = 'prototype development, improvements, integration, usability, and teamwork'; Final Round = 'functionality, final demonstration, user experience, market readiness, and implementation scope'. Winner-reported weightages (Team DORA, SIH1370 winner 2023): Round 1 = 20% (presentation, uniqueness, feasibility), Round 2 = 30% (tech & execution), Round 3 = 50% ('complete end-to-end product, commercial viability and end user perspective'). Jury explicitly checks whether mentoring-round suggestions were implemented by the next round. 2019 winner (HUL PS) describes a final 'power round' pitch as 'make or break'.

SCALE / NUMBERS: SIH 2024 released 254 PS (186 software + 68 hardware); max 500 idea submissions accepted per PS; 5-7 teams per PS reach the finale; ~44,000 teams nationally, ~57,000 ideas submitted (PM's Dec-2024 address: 7,000 ideas in 2017 -> 57,000 in 2024; ~14 lakh cumulative participants, 2 lakh+ teams, ~3,000 problems). Official 2024 results: 315 prize rows over 245 PS (177 'Winner', 128 'Joint Winner'). SIH 2023: 234 PS, 271 prize rows over 227 PS (202 software/69 hardware). SIH 2025: 322 prize rows over 268 PS (215 software/107 hardware), prize raised from Rs 1,00,000 to Rs 1,50,000 per PS; 60 nodal centres, 2,587 institutes took part in selection; SIH 2022 had 537 PS, 2,033 finalist teams at 75 nodal centres. AICTE 'MIC-Student Innovation' open-PS bucket is the biggest single winner pool every year (41 in 2023, 46 in 2024, 56 in 2025); NTRO (13-15/yr), Jal Shakti, Power, MoSJE, MHA/Police are the largest ministry pools.

COMPUTER-VISION / SURVEILLANCE WINNERS 2022 (DRDO cluster at ACS College of Engg, Bengaluru; official result PDF sih.gov.in/pdf/SIH-SOFTWARE-RESULT.pdf): NR1163 'Identification and rendering of human faces in videos on real time basis' -> Team Phantom# (Jaipur Engineering College & Research Centre, lead Siddharth Lodha); NR1165 'Solution to identify drones through CCTV feeds installed at houses, roads etc.' -> joint winners The Elite Unit (M S Ramaiah Inst. of Tech., lead Prakhar Awasthi) and Max Poolers (KLE Tech/Manav Rachna, lead Shivanand Kundargi); NR1167 gesture-enabled PC commands -> LAZZY PRO (Chennai Inst. of Tech.). 2022 also had a retail PS family ('Technological advances for Retail Outlets', Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas, AJ128/AJ129 in 2020 list) - winners not traced.

Patil IEMR Pune, AI&DS dept) and SIH1726 'aerial/drone images for construction progress' -> CodeZ (DJ Sanghvi, all 2nd-year IT students), both at IIT Gandhinagar; SIH1618 Delhi Govt 'online monitoring of unauthorized construction' -> joint Vajra (Thapar) & Indent (SRM Sonepat); SIH1719 MoSJE 'monitoring classroom sessions in skill training' -> TechSpectra (KK Wagh); SIH1752 India Post 'measurement & monitoring of counter services' (queue/service-time analytics) -> HexTech1 (MJCET Hyderabad); SIH1563/1565 NTRO SAR change detection & hyperspectral anomaly target detection -> HexaSAR_2024 (IIT Bombay) / Alt_24 (DJSCE EXTC); SIH1566 NDRF body detection in collapsed structures (HW) -> joint Shakti Group_CU1 & CODE-O-PHILES; SIH1705 Panchayati Raj feature extraction from drone orthophotos -> Future Fixers (KPRIET); Madhya Pradesh Police fielded 8 PS (SIH1783-1790) with 10 winners incl. 405_Resolved (DSCE), Trim Work (VIT-AP), Tech_Veda (IGDTUW) - titles not retrievable.

SIH25196 NSG 'Surveillance during extreme weather' (portable fog/haze/dark camera + human-size target ID + AR, HW) -> joint Impactx Innovators (UCE Kancheepuram) & feniX (Nachimuthu Polytechnic); SIH25165 Gujarat 'Temple & Pilgrimage Crowd Management (Somnath, Dwarka, Ambaji, Pavagadh)' -> Skip The Queue (IIT-ISM Dhanbad, lead Bhumi Bansal): public repo shows CatBoost+LightGBM (Optuna-tuned, stacked with Ridge) daily footfall forecaster using festival/holiday/weather/lag features, FastAPI /predict service, and YOLOv8 (.pt + ONNX) person detection + motion analytics classifying NORMAL/WARNING/PANIC with siren alarm on live feed; SIH25182 Coal/CMPDI 'Smart PPE compliance monitoring for underground mines' -> joint VEL MOTIVES (RMK) & CodeSolderRepeat (DJSCE); SIH25162 BEL 'Automated Optical Inspection based IC marking to identify fake marking' -> Win Diesel (DSCE), only 2 submissions; SIH25004/25005 DAHD 'Image-based cattle/buffalo breed recognition / animal type classification' -> A-6 (MIT-ADT Pune) and SkyNRG (IIT-ISM Dhanbad, aligned to Rashtriya Gokul Mission); SIH25012 Punjab 'Automated attendance system for rural schools' -> COGNISPHERE (KL Univ) and SIH25016 'Automated student attendance monitoring & analytics for colleges' -> ToinCoss/'AntiProxy' (DTU: 'dual-layer verification and intelligent classroom analytics' to kill proxy attendance); SIH25002 MoDoNER 'Smart Tourist Safety Monitoring & Incident Response using AI, Geo-fencing, Blockchain digital ID' -> ITerativebytes (DJSCE, final-year); SIH25050 Odisha 'Smart traffic management for urban congestion' -> Dynamo1 (Bennett); SIH25167 Chhattisgarh AI+IoT elephant movement detection -> joint ELECTROELITES & TrunkAlert; SIH25233 NTRO 'Automated VAPT tool for CCTV cameras & DVRs' -> Devillum (IIIT Kottayam); SIH25243 MoD underwater image enhancement -> NeuroBots; SIH25022 Railways 'AI-powered precise train traffic control' -> nyx (KJ Somaiya, national first prize, 500 finalist teams at WeSchool).

TEAM DORA (SIH1370, 2023, lead Dinesh A, DSCE; also won SIH'22 NR1174 as '01 Hum Bhi Bana Lenge') - fullest public post-mortem of a CV win: built AI+GIS infra-monitoring: CCTV day-over-day image comparison for progress %, material-consumption estimation from CCTV, milestone/task PM system, React-Native site-engineer app with photo-on-site-plan markup, Leaflet GIS map of all projects. Stack: ReactJS, NodeJS/Express, MongoDB, React Native, Leaflet, Flask + ML. PS-selection criteria they used: 'no dependencies, standalone solutions, fewer competitors, government not being the sole customer, monetization potential, large TAM, no hardware'. Spent '60% of time understanding the problem' (design thinking), validated with contractors/civil engineers. Jury R1 demanded inclusivity ('no user could find fault'), asked them to add air-quality monitoring and integration with other services; R2 demanded ML-model + frontend-backend integration and dynamic GIS; app broke 1 h before R3 (merge conflicts, code passed via WhatsApp); won anyway because 'all team members were involved in the pitch' and they put 'end to end implementation plan on BMC (Business Model Canvas)' - both 'earned brownie points'.

RADARVISION (SIH1606, 2024, DSCE) account (Chethan AC, Medium): won internal hackathon (50 -> 35 teams), then beat 150+ PPT submissions; at finale R1 evaluation 'not our best' -> implemented mentor feedback -> R2 'much better' -> R3 'falling into place'; lesson: 'just building a great product wasn't enough... showcase effectively, impress with innovation, sell the idea convincingly'. Team from a non-elite college beat 'top-tier colleges with senior students'. Note: Team Mystic Originals (IIIT Kota) pitched the same PS live to the PM (radar noise filtering -> time-frequency micro-Doppler -> ML, 'compact and cost-effective devices... highly scalable') yet did NOT win - PM facetime is not a predictor.

SARIKA PUROHIT (2022 winner, Govt of Jharkhand PS, team lead) - jury in R1 ACCUSED them of copying the frontend; rescued by showing original Figma designs. R2: judges handed a list of extra features; R3: integration broke hours before. Lessons: 'Presentation and storytelling matter as much as coding', 'Always take judges' feedback seriously', 'many teams who lost in the finals struggled mainly because of integration issues between frontend and backend... start integration from day one with testing', keep seniors/experts on standby, balanced team (2 ML, 3 backend, 1 full-stack).

PALAK (2023 winner, PS 1286 Ministry of Law & Justice, team 'insert_team_name'): ranked #1 of 437 idea submissions on their PS (only 6 selected); first mentoring round was 'a disappointment' because mentors expected an implementation the team hadn't planned; after implementing R1 asks, R2 judge was so impressed he took a photo with them; R3 pitch was cut short (7-min slot truncated) yet they still won - judges had already formed the view; team: 2 backend, 3 app devs, 1 ML.

JHANVI (2023 finalist, lost, AICTE PS 1458): explicit judge feedback - R1 mentors flagged missing authentication/security; judges told them to 'go in a flow while showing the prototype'; in R2 a chatbot connectivity glitch made judges 'visibly unappreciative' and judges said the UI/UX was 'too basic' and wanted 'a more professional look' ('we were under the idea that the idea is what matters more but we had a bitter realization'); final round carries 50%. PS with little research needed got 300-400 submissions; harder PS <150 - pick harder ones; 'keywords in PPT and abstract are a must'.

TANMAY BHATNAGAR (2019 winner, HUL track-and-trace PS): judges skeptical in R1/R2, told team to 'think more about how this will benefit the corporate and focus less on the tech'; overnight trained an ML model to bulk-scan QR codes from video (judges had said impossible) - impressed them in R3; 'judges were less concerned about the technology and more about the solution... every question was related to the solution and not the technology used'; constant informal contact with judges between rounds; VP Supply Chain HUL sat on the final jury.

ARINJAY PATHAK (2022 winner, DR716 legal keyword search, NLP): read all 530+ PS; avoided regional-language PS (no corpus); consulted a lawyer to understand e-courts; 'explore other problem statements of the same organisation... integrate solutions of similar PS into your own as novelty'; 'Implement suggestions by the judges'; 'You are being monitored - if your entire team sleeps the entire night, it gives off a bad impression'; 'Integration is the key... you are likely to surpass most competitors if all functionalities are integrated and working'; one presenter only; tie-break rule favours team with more female members; PPT must not contain screenshots of pre-built code (coding allowed only during finale).

SHIVAM CHAUDHARY (2022 winner DR716, GIET Gunupur): Django REST + Next.js; mentors pushed to 'innovate a unique solution to a single problem from a whole bunch of problems'; final report covered future aspects and revenue model; judges' implicit questions: purpose, audience, how data gets populated, how revenue is generated, future roadmap.

JUDGE/ORGANISER STATEMENTS ON WHAT WINS: WeSchool-Mumbai nodal judge Dr Yogesh Topale (2024): winners 'gave prototype output very close to the problem statement requirements'. GeeksforGeeks 2023 finalist: judges asked about 'prototype, the quality of your data, how well your prototype works, its scalability, practical applications, estimated costs, and development time'. SPSU AvaGuardians (2023 MoD avalanche PS) were judged by 'scientists from the Ministry of Defence' and earned a 6-week DRDO internship. SIH testimonials page: Exalt (2018 AYUSH) 'chatbot was very new technological implementation which impressed judges'; GEN-Y (MoSPI CPI app) got real deployment on NIC servers; PM 2024 speech cites past SIH solutions integrated with ISRO (cyclone-intensity system, video geotagging) and used by NDRF (blood-bank system) - implementability in a ministry is the stated end-goal, and MoE guidelines fund post-SIH implementation (Rs 10-15k/month stipend, 6-12 months, ministry mentor, quarterly reports).

PM MODI'S EMPHASES (Dec 2024 address, proxy for government/judge values): 'local need-based solutions for Bharat's requirements... but their application and impact are global'; asked teams whether they had met real users (autism centres), spoke to ISRO scientists, how it helps during Kumbh Mela (40-45 crore people); praised 'completely offline' cyber solution, 'compact and cost-effective devices... highly scalable', federated learning for Ganga (38 stations, local models + mother model, stakeholder dashboard with one-click 'report' to authorities); asked drone-classifier team if they can also give range/direction/speed (i.e. pushes beyond the PS minimum).

RECURRING PATTERNS THAT WIN (synthesised from all winner accounts + rubric): (1) fully INTEGRATED end-to-end demo (ML + backend + frontend + mobile/GIS) - integration failure is the #1 stated cause of losing; (2) visibly implementing each mentoring round's asks before the next evaluation; (3) polished, professional UI/UX - judges penalise basic UI even with a good idea; (4) business framing: Business Model Canvas, revenue model, TAM, customers beyond government, cost & dev-time estimates; (5) end-user/Indian-context research (talked to lawyers, contractors, autism centres, border residents) and inclusivity; (6) scalability + low cost + offline/edge capability + integration with existing government systems/data (existing CCTV network, DWLR data, e-courts, Namami Gange open data); (7) going beyond the PS (adding adjacent PS features, extra metrics like air quality); (8) confident storytelling pitch with one main presenter but every member able to defend their module; (9) novelty that is defensible (original Figma, own models) - plagiarism suspicion is actively probed; (10) feasibility within 36 h - pick PS matching team skills, avoid hardware/dependency-heavy PS.

COMPETITION-DENSITY DATA: CV/defence/security PS attract far fewer idea submissions than 'easy' ones (sih-nav 2025 counts: SIH25162 AOI IC marking 2, SIH25196 extreme-weather surveillance 8, SIH25197 NSG video analytics 12, SIH25182 PPE monitoring 7, SIH25165 temple crowd 51, vs generic AICTE/education PS 300-500). Winners repeatedly advise choosing under-subscribed, research-heavy PS from ministries/PSUs (BEL, NTRO, DRDO, NSG, ISRO) where domain depth beats polish competition.

REPEAT-WINNER / COLLEGE EFFECTS: same DJSCE teams won two years running (INNOV8_01 SIH1714 2024 -> INNOV_01 SIH25033 2025; Linear_Depression SIH1661 2024 -> SIH25006 2025); DSCE Bengaluru produced DORA (2022, 2023), RadarVision (2024), 405_Resolved, Win Diesel (2025); Mahindra University won DRDO CV PS 4 consecutive years; Kongu Engg College 5 wins in 2024. Strong college SIH culture (internal hackathon rigour, alumni mentoring, SPOC support) is a visible predictor. Teams of 6 with mandatory female member; typical winning composition 2 ML + 2 backend + 2 frontend/UI-presentation, often 2nd-3rd year students.

TECH STACKS SEEN IN WINNING CV/AI SOLUTIONS: YOLOv5/v8 (+ONNX export) for person/object/PPE/drone detection; ResNet50/CNN classifiers; OpenCV motion analytics; CatBoost/LightGBM/Optuna for footfall forecasting; Flask/FastAPI inference services; React/Next.js + Node/Express or Django REST backends; MongoDB/Firebase; React Native/Flutter apps; Leaflet/GIS; Electron desktop (NALCO 2024 winner: Electron+React+TS+Zustand, FastAPI, scikit-learn/TensorFlow); federated learning & offline-first/PWA architectures (MaternitySafe, NEXAURA2.3 'offline-first agricultural advisory' 2025 winner, SIKSHALOG offline-first attendance); blockchain only as an adjunct (tourist digital ID). Real sensor/CCTV data in the demo beats slides.

PS-SELECTION SIGNALS FOR A RETAIL/SURVEILLANCE/EDGE-AI ENTRY: precedent winners exist for e-commerce image QC (SIH1358 2023), CCTV crowd/crime/work monitoring on existing railway cameras (SIH1349 2023, joint win), counter-service time monitoring (SIH1752 2024), women-safety video analytics (SIH1605 2024), temple footfall+panic detection (SIH25165 2025), PPE compliance (SIH25182 2025), NSG video interpretation (SIH25197 2025), attendance/proxy analytics (SIH25012/25016 2025) - judges in these tracks consistently rewarded: reuse of EXISTING camera infrastructure (no new hardware), real-time alerts with escalation to authorities, dashboards for multiple stakeholder roles, hotspot/heatmap analytics, privacy-respecting design, low-cost/edge deployability, and measurable KPIs (accuracy %, latency, footfall forecasts).

PROCESS FACTS USEFUL FOR STRATEGY: idea-PPT round is evaluated blind by SIH/ministry reviewers (ranking within PS visible - Palak's team listed first); top 5-7 per PS go to finale; allowed to submit ideas for multiple PS (since 2023); winners then offered ministry internships/implementation; tie-break favours more female members; 2025 finale = 8-9 Dec software (36 h), 8-12 Dec hardware (IIT Roorkee); 2024 finale 11-12 Dec; 2023 finale 19-20 Dec; 2022 finale 25-26 Aug; jury briefing + 3 rounds (R1 evening day-1, R2 morning day-2, final 5:30-7 pm day-2).

topic: Official SIH 2024/2025 Idea Presentation PPT template format, portal/internal-hackathon submission fields, evaluation criteria, and finalist/mentor tips for filling each slide
findings: OFFICIAL TEMPLATE DOWNLOADS (verified live, HTTP 200 on 2026-08-23): SIH2025 = https://www.sih.gov.in/letters/SIH2025-IDEA-Presentation-Format.pptx (271 KB); SIH2024 = https://www.sih.gov.in/letters/SIH2024_IDEA_Presentation_Format.pptx (291 KB); legacy SIH2020 'Idea ppt.pptx' = https://www.sih.gov.in/letters/Idea%20ppt.pptx. Both 2024 and 2025 decks are 16:9 (12192000x6858000 EMU = 13.33in x 7.5in), 7 slides (6 content + 1 instructions slide to delete). The 2024 and 2025 templates are textually IDENTICAL except the year on the title slide.

OFFICIAL TEMPLATE SLIDE 1 (verbatim, extracted from pptx XML): heading 'TITLE PAGE' / 'SMART INDIA HACKATHON 2025'; fields: 'Problem Statement ID -', 'Problem Statement Title-', 'Theme-', 'PS Category- Software/Hardware', 'Team ID-', 'Team Name (Registered on portal)'.

OFFICIAL TEMPLATE SLIDE 2 (verbatim): heading 'IDEA TITLE'; subheading 'Proposed Solution (Describe your Idea/Solution/Prototype)'; pointers: 'Detailed explanation of the proposed solution', 'How it addresses the problem', 'Innovation and uniqueness of the solution'. Footer on every content slide: slide number, '@SIH Idea submission- Template', 'Your Team Name'.

OFFICIAL TEMPLATE SLIDE 3 (verbatim): heading 'TECHNICAL APPROACH'; pointers: 'Technologies to be used (e.g. programming languages, frameworks, hardware)', 'Methodology and process for implementation (Flow Charts/Images/ working prototype)'.

OFFICIAL TEMPLATE SLIDE 4 (verbatim): heading 'FEASIBILITY AND VIABILITY'; pointers: 'Analysis of the feasibility of the idea', 'Potential challenges and risks', 'Strategies for overcoming these challenges'.
OFFICIAL TEMPLATE SLIDE 5 (verbatim): heading 'IMPACT AND BENEFITS'; pointers: 'Potential impact on the target audience', 'Benefits of the solution (social, economic, environmental, etc.)'.
OFFICIAL TEMPLATE SLIDE 6 (verbatim): heading 'RESEARCH  AND REFERENCES'; pointer: 'Details / Links of the reference and research work'.

OFFICIAL TEMPLATE SLIDE 7 'IMPORTANT INSTRUCTIONS' (verbatim): 'Please ensure below pointers are met while submitting the Idea PPT: (1) Kindly keep the maximum slides limit up to six (6). (Including the title slide) (2) Try to avoid paragraphs and post your idea in points /diagrams / Infographics /pictures (3) Keep your explanation precise and easy to understand (4) Idea should be unique and novel. (5) You can only use provided template for making the PPT without changing the idea details pointers (mentioned in previous slides). (6) You need to save the file in PDF and upload the same on portal. No PPT, Word Doc or any other format will be supported. Note - You can delete this slide (Important Pointers) when you upload the details of your idea on SIH portal.' No explicit word limit exists anywhere in the official template or guidelines -- only 'avoid paragraphs' and 6-slide cap.

LEGACY SIH2020 TEMPLATE (https://www.sih.gov.in/letters/Idea%20ppt.pptx) had 3 slides: (1) 'Idea/Approach Details' with Ministry/Organization name, Problem Statement, Team Name, Team Leader Name, College Code; (2) 'Describe your idea / Solution / Prototype here' + 'Describe your Technology stack here'; (3) 'Describe your Use Cases here' + 'Describe your Dependencies / Show stopper here'. This is why many winning decks and coaching guides still include a Use-Cases-by-stakeholder block and a Dependencies/Showstoppers block even though the 2024/2025 template does not ask for them.

SIH PORTAL IDEA SUBMISSION FIELDS (verbatim from official SIH2025-Guidelines-College-SPOC.pdf, p.11, https://www.sih.gov.in/letters/SIH2025-Guidelines-College-SPOC.pdf; updated copy at https://sih.gov.in/letters/SIH2025-Guidelines-College-SPOC-updated.pdf): 'The team leader needs to enter the details on the SIH portal that include: 1) Verify pre-entered Team name. 2) Verify pre-entered College authorization letter PDF (in given format) 3) Verify pre-entered Names of team leader and the rest 5 team members 4) Verify pre-entered Gender ... 5) Verify pre-entered Email id ... 6) Verify pre-entered Mobile no. ... 7) Chosen problem statement or Student Innovation Category. 8) Idea title. 9) Idea description. 10) Idea presentation (PDF).' SPOC uploads team details (Annexure A) first; team leader then gets login credentials to complete idea submission.

OFFICIAL IDEA SELECTION CRITERIA (verbatim, SIH2025 guidelines p.13; identical wording in SIH2020 FAQ PDF https://www.sih.gov.in/pdf/IdeasubmissionprocessSIH2020.pdf): 'Post Idea submission process, the ideas will be evaluated by experts. Evaluation criteria will include novelty of the idea, complexity, clarity and details in the prescribed format, feasibility, practicability, sustainability, scale of impact, user experience and potential for future work progression.' Note 'clarity and details in the prescribed format' is itself a scored criterion -- changing the template pointers costs marks.

SIH2025 PROCESS RULES (official guidelines): SPOC registration from Aug 2025; last date for team nomination + idea submission by SPOC and team leader = 30 Sept 2025; 'only 300 ideas will be submitted for a particular PS' then the PS freezes (live counter shown next to each PS on sih.gov.in); 'One team can submit Ideas against maximum of 2 Problem Statement only'; max 50 teams per institute (45 shortlisted + 5 waitlisted), 100 per university; team = exactly 6 incl. leader, at least 1 female, all same college; team name must be unique and must not contain institute name; '4-5 teams per problem statement may be selected for the grand finale'; Grand Finale offline at nodal centres, 2nd/3rd week Dec 2025; prize Rs 1,50,000 per PS; ideas 'must be new and must not have been present in any previous event/program of any sort'.

INTERNAL HACKATHON -- WHAT THE SPOC MUST UPLOAD (official guidelines p.5-6): Internal Hackathon Report (max 15 pages: event overview 1p, photos 2p, participating teams' pictures 2p, judging process 1p, jury panel details 1p, nominated top teams 1p, judges' info 1p, total teams & students 2p, news articles 1p, social media promotion 1p with #sih2025 #smartindiahackathon2025), Image/Video link, Location, Date, Mode (Online/Offline), Total teams, Total students, Female count, Male count. FAQ (https://www.sih.gov.in/faqs): internal hackathon is mandatory; institutes may use their own PS; 'Each team can submit only two ideas'; students submit only after SPOC nomination.

INTERNAL HACKATHON SUBMISSION FORMS AT COLLEGES typically ask for: Idea PPT 'in the prescribed format shared by organizers' (the official SIH template, exported to PDF), Problem Statement Title 'with SIH PS ID, if applicable, or Open Innovation', and optionally a 'Prototype/Demo Link (GitHub repo, screenshots, or demo video)' (RECABN Devpost: https://sih-recabn.devpost.com/). IGNOU's internal form (https://www.ignou.ac.in/viewFile/NCIDE/notification/General_Guidelines-SIH_2025.pdf) asks: Idea Title, Idea Description, Idea PPT in PDF Format, team leader + 5 members with mobile, enrollment no., email, programme, year, address, regional centre. XIE/RJIT forms: member names, gender, email, mobile, stream, year of study, optional mentor, PS title (https://www.scribd.com/document/898399167/SIH-XIE-Internal-Hackathon-Registration-Form-2025 ; https://rjit.ac.in/sih2025/). Pitch slot commonly 3 minutes + Q&A.

INTERNAL HACKATHON JUDGING RUBRICS SEEN: RECABN Devpost -- Innovation & Creativity, Relevance to Problem Statement, Technical Implementation, Impact & Scalability, Presentation & Communication (3-minute pitch). 'SIH'25 Evaluation Criteria' doc (https://www.scribd.com/document/915964336/SIH-25-Evaluation-Criteria) -- Problem Understanding, Novelty, Technical Depth and Feasibility, Presentation and Communication, Social Relevance and Impact, Preparedness and Past Work; 'a prototype demo can be optional for bonus marks or mandatory as an additional criterion'. NorthCap Univ internal report reused the official national criteria verbatim (novelty, complexity, clarity, adherence to format, feasibility, practicability, sustainability, impact scale, UX, future development).

HOW WINNING DECKS STRUCTURE SLIDE 2 (Idea/Proposed Solution) -- from 'Guide to Create a Winning PPT' by SIH winner team Hack4Justice (Walchand College, PS SIH1280 AICTE e-Portal for case management), distributed via Let's Code (guide: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1aRGERc4nAMPij6wYJWBOiZoFTCnq9s0g/view ; sample deck: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1e6g0r1NYsiQ4MsKcaxEY9HlMLxuabFBS/view ; blog: https://www.lets-code.co.in/blogs/sih-2025-complete-guide-ppt-template/): 'Straight to the point'; 'Every bullet point explained impact in simple language'; 'Avoided jargon overload'. Mistakes: 'Writing solution in a paragraph form - judges get bored'; 'Only showing features without linking to problem solved'; 'Adding 10+ features instead of focusing on 3-4 solid ones'.

HOW WINNING DECKS DO THE PROCESS FLOWCHART (same guide): 'Showed how a user actually interacts (upload docs -> AI explains -> guidance -> lawyer connect)'; 'Simple, visual, step-wise flow - easy for judges to imagine usage'; include one concrete example (they used 'divorce papers'). Mistakes: 'Overcomplicated diagrams with 20 arrows'; 'Keeping it abstract - without a real example'. The sample winning deck puts a left-column process flow chart next to the idea bullets, and a separate Technology Stack column listing exact tools (Hugging Face Transformers, LexNLP + spaCy, Elasticsearch, Neo4j, AES-256 + Blockchain audit, Docker/Kubernetes).

HOW WINNING DECKS DO TECH STACK (same guide): 'We listed specific tools ... Judges love clarity'; 'Showed scalability (Docker/Kubernetes) - proves we thought of real-world deployment'; 'Didn't just say AI/ML - instead, named exact frameworks'. Mistakes: 'Writing Python, AI, Cloud - too generic'; 'Adding unnecessary tech that they don't actually know'; 'Not aligning tech stack with the problem'.

HOW WINNING DECKS DO USE CASES + DEPENDENCIES/SHOWSTOPPERS (same guide; map these onto the 2025 'Feasibility and Viability' slide): use cases 'Divided into Client, Advocate, Judge/Admin - directly mapped to SIH stakeholders'; 'Each use case showed benefit, not just feature'; mistakes: 'generic use cases like everyone can use it', 'Missing the government/judge perspective (important in SIH)'. Dependencies: 'We were honest about challenges (trust, government cooperation, quality data)'; 'Judges appreciate teams that know real hurdles'; mistakes: 'Writing no showstoppers - unrealistic', 'Not thinking about legal/data constraints'.

WINNER'S 'PPT MUST DO CHECKLIST' (same guide, verbatim): 'Idea - Is my idea clearly defined and relevant to the problem statement? Solution - Does my solution effectively solve the identified problem? Flow Chart - Have I shown the step-by-step process clearly? Tech Stack - Did I mention the right tools, frameworks, and technologies? Prototype - Have I included a working demo or mockup to showcase? Feasibility & Viability - Can this be realistically built and sustained? Impact & Benefits - Have I highlighted who benefits and how big the impact is? Research & References - Did I back my idea with proper research/data?' CONTESTED TIP ON PROTOTYPE SCREENSHOTS: the official template itself invites 'Flow Charts/Images/ working prototype' on the Technical Approach slide, winners (CODESTRIX '80% built', Hack4Justice checklist 'Prototype - working demo or mockup') include prototype status/mockups, and many internal hackathons award bonus marks for a demo link. topic: Computer vision for shelf/inventory monitoring (OOS gap detection, SKU-110K, planogram compliance, shelf segmentation, few-shot/CLIP product recognition, open models, commercial vendors) and queue analytics (queue length estimation, wait-time prediction, congestion forecasting, real-world deployments)
findings: SKU-110K (Goldman et al., CVPR 2019 'Precise Detection in Densely Packed Scenes'): 11,743 shelf images (8,219 train / 588 val / 2,936 test), single class 'object', ~1.7M boxes, avg ~147 boxes/image; '110K' = number of unique SKUs pictured, NOT classes. Ultralytics ships it as `SKU-110K.yaml` (train with `YOLO('yolo26n.pt').train(data='SKU-110K.yaml', epochs=100, imgsz=640)`). Paper contributions: Soft-IoU layer + EM-Merger (Mixture of Gaussians NMS replacement) on keras-retinanet; pretrained weights + data on GitHub eg4000/SKU110K_CVPR19 (AWS S3 SKU110K_fixed.tar.gz). HF mirrors: Voxel51/sku110k_test, PrashantDixit0/SKU-110K. URLs: https://docs.ultralytics.com/datasets/detect/sku-110k , https://github.com/eg4000/SKU110K_CVPR19 , https://arxiv.org/pdf/1904.00853

Open-source OOS/empty-shelf datasets on Roboflow Universe (all bounding-box, single 'empty space' style class): 'Out Of Stock detection' by Empty Space Detection Capstone = 1,013 images (class Empty-Space) https://universe.roboflow.com/empty-space-detection-capstone/out-of-stock-detection ; 'Supermarket Empty Shelf Detector' by FYP = 497 images (class Out-of-Stock-Instances) https://universe.roboflow.com/fyp-ormnr/supermarket-empty-shelf-detector ; 'Empty Shelf Detector' by FYP = 198 images https://universe.roboflow.com/fyp-ormnr/empty-shelf-detector ; 'empty shelf detection' by Policenta = 1,050 images (class Empty-space) used in Roboflow blog; 'Empty Spaces Detection in Shelf Data' by DSJourney https://universe.roboflow.com/dsjourney/empty-spaces-detection-in-shelf-data ; 'out of stock' by study = 114 images. Roboflow search: https://universe.roboflow.com/search?q=class%3Aempty

Roboflow reference pipeline for empty-shelf tracking (https://blog.roboflow.com/retail-store-object-detection/): RF-DETR (Small) trained on 1,050-image Policenta dataset, confidence threshold 0.4; status logic = sum(bbox areas)/image area -> 'Stocked' if 0 detections, 'Partially stocked' if coverage <20%, 'Empty' if coverage >=20%; emits JSON (detection count, bbox area, coverage %) + annotated image via Roboflow Workflows. Training on hosted infra ~30-45 min.

Hugging Face open models for shelves: foduucom/product-detection-in-shelf-yolov8 (YOLOv8, 2 classes 'Empty Shelves' and 'Magical Products' i.e. stocked, self-reported box mAP@0.5 = 0.910, no license stated) https://huggingface.co/foduucom/product-detection-in-shelf-yolov8 ; wiwiewei18/smart-shelf-tracker (YOLO11n fine-tuned on 497-image Roboflow 'Retail Empty Shelf Detector', class OOS, 640x640, metrics not reported) https://huggingface.co/wiwiewei18/smart-shelf-tracker

Peer-reviewed OOS detector (Sensors 2024, 'Enhanced Out-of-Stock Detection in Retail Shelf Images Based on Deep Learning', https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10819825/): 511 shelf images from 4 Croatian retailers, 1,210 OOS instances in 2 classes ('normal' fully empty = 730, 'front' partially empty = 480). Models YOLOv5s6 / YOLOv7-tiny / EfficientDet-D3. Novel 'OOS mirroring' augmentation (duplicate + horizontally mirror OOS instances over neighbors), two-stage train (pretrain on augmented, finetune on originals), aspect-ratio post-filter per store section. 5-fold CV results: YOLOv5 mAP 85.0% (normal 86.3 / front 83.7), YOLOv7 83.0%, EfficientDet 80.4%; +1.6-2.3 mAP from two-stage training, +1.2-2.5 from post-processing; 7-17 ms/image on GPU, intended for once-per-minute shelf checks.

Industrial real-time empty-shelf pipeline (arXiv 2205.13060, 'Designing an Efficient End-to-end ML Pipeline for Real-time Empty-shelf Detection', https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.13060): 1,000 images collected/annotated under strict guidelines; mean average F1 68.5%; throughput 67 img/s on Intel Xeon Gold CPU and 860 img/s on A100 after runtime optimization. Emphasizes that annotation guidelines (what counts as a gap) dominate accuracy.

Robot-based OOS detection: 'Deep learning based empty shelf detection based on autonomous mobile robot' (CVIU 2026, https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1077314226000640) uses a two-stage Segmenter-ViT (shelf segmentation) + YOLOv6 (gap detection) pipeline to suppress false positives: 90.86% F1 on empty shelves, 93.00% navigation success, ROS platform, ~9x faster than human auditors. Predecessor: De Simone et al., ICCVW 2023 'Autonomous mobile robot for automatic out of stock detection in a supermarket' https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content/ICCV2023W/ACVR/papers/De_Simone_Autonomous_Mobile_Robot_for_Automatic_out_of_Stock_Detection_in_ICCVW_2023_paper.pdf

Shelf segmentation / row detection: 'Shelf Management: a deep learning-based system for shelf visual monitoring' (Expert Systems with Applications vol 255, 2024, doi 10.1016/j.eswa.2024.124635; code+data https://github.com/rokopi-byte/shelf_management). 3-stage pipeline: RetinaNet product detection (0.752 mAP) -> Deep Hough Transform for shelf rows as semantic lines (97% F1) -> MobileNetV3 embedding trained with triplet loss + FAISS nearest-neighbor product recognition (93% top-1). Releases two datasets: SHARD (SHelf mAnagement Row Dataset) and SHAPE (SHelf mAnagement Product dataset) on figshare. Follow-up 'Retail Shelf Monitoring Using Deep Hough Transform and Object Detection' (SciTePress 2026) derives gaps from product boxes vs. detected row lines: https://www.scitepress.org/Papers/2026/143457/143457.pdf . Classical baseline: Sobel vertical-gradient image + Hough horizontal lines, 83.4% on 229 shelf images (Varol & Kuzu 'Toward retail product recognition on grocery shelves').

Planogram compliance methods: (a) MDPI Applied Sciences 13(18):10145 'Computer Vision Based Planogram Compliance Evaluation' — Gaussian-layer-network product proposals + Domain Invariant Hierarchical Embedding (DIHE) classifier + RANSAC pose estimation vs planogram; evaluated on GP-180 and a Nordic-retailer dataset https://www.mdpi.com/2076-3417/13/18/10145 ; (b) Scientific Reports 2025 'Real-time retail planogram compliance application using computer vision and virtual shelves' — shelf detection + product recognition + multi-image stitching into 'virtual shelves' + custom alignment algorithm vs digital planogram https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-025-27773-5 ; (c) mobile on-prem system YOLOv7 detection + EfficientNetV2B1 classification, product detection accuracy up to 96.3% (Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services 2026, https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0969698926001050); (d) FAN-transformer few-shot product recognition: 98.39% top-1 / 99.48% top-5 on unseen products with 5 samples/class (ResearchGate 395813687). (e) Roboflow 'Planogram Compliance Detection' tutorial uses RF-DETR for empty zones + Gemini 2.5 Flash VLM prompted to return JSON (brand, row, facing count, position) then rule checks (brand blocking, facing counts, gaps) — no predefined planogram https://blog.roboflow.com/planogram-compliance-detection/

Few-shot / embedding-based product recognition (add new SKUs without retraining): RetailKLIP (arXiv 2312.10282) finetunes OpenCLIP ViT-L/14 (LAION-2B) with ArcFace loss (pytorch-metric-learning) on in-house RP6K (~1M images, 6,500 products, long-tail) on a single GTX 1080Ti; zero-shot nearest-neighbor accuracy: CAPG-GP 88.6%, Grozi-120 82.8%, RP2K 87.7% https://arxiv.org/html/2312.10282 . 'Exploring Fine-grained Retail Product Discrimination with Zero-shot Object Classification Using VLMs' (arXiv 2409.14963): MIMEX dataset 28 classes (10,357 train / 4,920 test); CLIP ViT-B/32 text-prompt zero-shot only 40-42% (~60% with BLIP-2 captions); CLIP visual-prototype k-NN (k=11) 89.0% (93.9% cleaned), 89.9% with only 50 samples/class; ensemble CLIP+DINOv2+PCA(512) 92.0-92.2%. Practitioner pattern (Width.ai 2026): YOLOv11/RT-DETR detector + CLIP/DINOv2 embeddings + vector DB (FAISS/Milvus/Pinecone) cosine NN https://www.width.ai/post/product-recognition

Retail product datasets for recognition/fine-tuning: Grozi-120 (120 products, 676 studio + 4,973 in-store video frames), GroZi-3.2k, Grocery Products (80 categories), RP2K (>500k shelf images, ~2,388 products, https://arxiv.org/pdf/2006.12634), Products-10K (~10k classes, ~150k images), RPC checkout dataset (200 categories, 83,739 images), Products-6K, Retail-786k (visual entity matching, https://arxiv.org/html/2309.17164v2), CAPG-GP, MIMEX (28 classes), SHARD/SHAPE (shelf rows/products).

Amazon Just Walk Out — ceiling-rail RGB cameras + load-cell weight sensors front/back of each shelf, head/hand tracking, 3D store maps from iPad LiDAR; 2024 shift from chained models to a single multi-modal transformer that 'generates a receipt instead of text'; inference on Amazon-built on-prem edge devices; Amazon closed its own 72 Go/Fresh stores in early 2026 but licenses JWO to third parties/stadiums. https://venturebeat.com/ai/inside-amazons-new-just-walk-out-ai-transformers-meets-edge-computing , https://www.aboutamazon.com/news/retail/amazon-just-walk-out-improves-accuracy

Queue length estimation (CV): standard recipe = person detector (YOLO11/YOLO26, RF-DETR) + tracker (ByteTrack/BoT-SORT) + polygon ROI; count track IDs whose bbox center passes cv2.pointPolygonTest inside the zone; dwell = (exit_frame - entry_frame)/fps. Ultralytics ships `solutions.QueueManager(model='yolo26n.pt', region=[(x,y)...], line_width, show)` that counts objects remaining in region per frame https://docs.ultralytics.com/guides/queue-management . Roboflow tutorial uses RF-DETR via `inference` + `supervision` PolygonZone, logs per-person and average wait to CSV https://blog.roboflow.com/monitor-retail-queues/ . Roboflow datasets: QueueIQ https://universe.roboflow.com/queueiq/queueiq , crowd counting (2,898 images) https://universe.roboflow.com/crowd-dataset/crowd-counting-dataset-w3o7w , people_counting (846 images) https://universe.roboflow.com/people-counting/people_counting

Detection vs density-map counting: detection-based (YOLO/Faster R-CNN) counting degrades under heavy occlusion/dense crowds; density-map regression (CSRNet: dilated convs on VGG backbone) is dominant for congested scenes; rule of thumb — light occlusion: detect heads/persons; heavy occlusion: density map. Surveys: https://github.com/gjy3035/Awesome-Crowd-Counting , https://ietresearch.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1049/ipr2.13328

Real-world CV queue deployment (Ultralytics case study, Cali Intelligence): YOLO medium->small on edge servers, 8 retail sites; average queue length 7 -> 4 customers (43% reduction) in two weeks; miss rate <6%; alert accuracy >90%; cut unnecessary till openings by 10% off-peak; queue-length forecast MAE 0.8 customers, predicts build-up up to 15 min ahead; alerts when queue threshold exceeded, integrates with VMS. https://www.ultralytics.com/customers/cali-intelligence-cuts-retail-checkout-queues-with-ultralytics-yolo

Wait-time prediction ML (IEEE 2024/25 'Waiting Time Prediction in Queue Management: Leveraging Machine Learning Approach', https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/document/10955915/): compared regression algorithms and LSTM; best = Voting Regressor ensemble with R2 0.944 and MAE 1.828 minutes. ICCSA 2023 'Predicting Multiple Domain Queue Waiting Time via ML' (https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1007/978-3-031-36805-9_27): CRISP-DM on millions of ticket-system records across banks/pharmacies, 5 regression algorithms with different feature sets. UCF NCA paper: LSTM predicting next-cycle queue length from queue length + wait time history https://www.cecs.ucf.edu/shasan/wp-content/uploads/2021/09/Queue_Length_Prediction_Accepted_Version_NCA.pdf . Simple baseline: Little's Law L = lambda*W -> W = L/lambda (queue count / measured arrival or service rate), distribution-free. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Little's_law

Congestion/footfall forecasting method comparisons: BiLSTM vs ARIMA on weekly retail demand cut RMSE/MAE up to 42.35%/40.10% (https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2352146526002851); multiple ARIMA vs Prophet vs LSTM studies show LSTM lowest error (e.g., MAE 21.69 / RMSE 29.96 in one comparison, https://thescipub.com/pdf/jcssp.2024.1222.1230.pdf), Prophet second with 83.8% interval coverage in retail demand; SARIMA typically worst. Practical stack for hackathon-scale: Prophet/SARIMA for hour-of-day x day-of-week seasonality, gradient boosting/voting regressor on lag + calendar features, LSTM if >weeks of minute-level data.

Tesco + Irisys (since 2006, >1,000 UK stores): ceiling-mounted thermal/infrared people counters at entrances plus IR sensors above each till count 'units' of shoppers (group-vs-individual logic) and wait time; algorithm predicts optimal number of open tills 5/10/15/30 minutes ahead, underpinning Tesco's 'One in Front' promise (open another till if >1 person waiting). findings: STORE-AND-FORWARD (AWS Greengrass v2 Stream Manager): per-stream policy with maxSize default 256 MB (min 1 KB), strategyOnFull = RejectNewData | OverwriteOldestData, persistence = File (survives restarts) | Memory, per-stream export priority so critical streams flush first on reconnect; exports to Kinesis Data Streams, IoT SiteWise, S3 (IoT Analytics discontinued 15 Dec 2025). Runtime params: STREAM_MANAGER_EXPORTER_MAX_BANDWIDTH (kbps, default unlimited), EXPORTER_THREAD_POOL_SIZE default 5, S3 multipart min part 5,242,880 bytes, server port 8088, store dir /greengrass/v2/work/aws.greengrass.StreamManager. Needs >=70 MB extra RAM + Java. Data at rest on edge is NOT encrypted by Greengrass (relies on FS perms/FDE). Greengrass core pricing $0.16/active device/month; first 3 core devices free for 12 months. STORE-AND-FORWARD (Azure IoT Edge 1.6 LTS): edgeHub buffers all device-to-cloud messages while offline and replays in original order on reconnect; devices can run offline indefinitely after one initial sync; default message TTL (storeAndForwardConfiguration.timeToLiveSecs) = 7,200 s (2 h), max ~2^31 s; storage bounded by disk; must map host storage into edgeHub/edgeAgent for durability (container FS is ephemeral by default); parent gateway supports up to 100 child devices by default (MaxConnectedClients); known blind spot: portal can still show '200 OK' while the device is actually offline. IoT Edge runtime itself is free; IoT Hub free tier = 8,000 msgs/day, 500 devices. Layered/automatic deployments use twin-tag target conditions + priority (layered must have higher priority than base). URLs: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/iot-edge/offline-capabilities , https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/iot-edge/how-to-deploy-at-scale , https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/pricing/details/iot-edge/

MQTT for flaky links: only QoS 1/2 messages are queued by the broker for disconnected clients, and only with a persistent session (cleanSession=false / MQTT5 Clean Start=0 + Session Expiry Interval in seconds, max 4,294,967,295 s). MQTT 5 adds per-PUBLISH Message Expiry Interval so stale telemetry self-drops from offline queues. Client libraries must locally persist unacked outbound QoS1/2 messages (flash buffering in Azure SDK, Greengrass, Zephyr). Greengrass legacy broker holds max 100 in-flight QoS1 msgs to IoT Core before waiting for ACK. Guidance: QoS0 for high-frequency non-critical telemetry, QoS1 default, QoS2 for commands/transactions; QoS1 implies at-least-once so consumers need idempotency keys. URLs: https://www.hivemq.com/blog/mqtt-essentials-part-7-persistent-session-queuing-messages/ , https://www.hivemq.com/blog/mqtt5-essentials-part4-session-and-message-expiry/ , https://www.emqx.com/en/blog/mqtt-session , https://docs.aws.amazon.com/iot/latest/developerguide/mqtt.html

SQLite WAL on the edge node: readers never block the single writer and vice-versa (ideal for a POS UI thread + background outbox/sync worker); auto-checkpoint default wal_autocheckpoint=1000 pages (~4 MB); PRAGMA synchronous=NORMAL skips fsync on each commit (only at checkpoint) so last transactions can roll back on power loss - use FULL for sales records in an outage-prone environment; WAL does NOT work on network filesystems (needs shared-memory wal-index); transactions >100 MB not optimal, >1 GB may fail; long-lived readers cause checkpoint starvation / unbounded -wal growth (mitigate with SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_RESTART/TRUNCATE and reader gaps). URL: https://www.sqlite.org/wal.html

OUTBOX + IDEMPOTENCY pattern for edge->cloud: write business row and outbox event in one local SQLite transaction, relay polls outbox (typical 10-50 ms interval, adds low tens of ms latency), cloud consumer dedups on event_id via control table kept 24-72 h; yields at-least-once with effectively-once processing. AWS Prescriptive Guidance doc: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/prescriptive-guidance/latest/cloud-design-patterns/transactional-outbox.html ; https://event-driven.io/en/outbox_inbox_patterns_and_delivery_guarantees_explained/ ; https://milanjovanovic.tech/blog/implementing-the-outbox-pattern

CRDT / conflict resolution: sqlite-sync (sqliteai) adds CRDT replication to ordinary SQLite tables (Add-Wins, Delete-Wins, Causal-Length Set, Grow-Only, line-level text merge), syncs to SQLite Cloud/Postgres/Supabase - https://github.com/sqliteai/sqlite-sync . PN-counters (Redis CRDT, Couchbase) are the canonical CRDT for stock counts (merge = max per-node P and N, value = sum P - sum N) BUT cannot enforce non-negative inventory invariants across replicas; recommended hybrid = CRDT/LWW for catalog+metadata, append-only event ledger (sale/receipt events with HLC timestamps) for stock, authoritative recompute in cloud. KubeEdge (CNCF): EdgeCore single binary ~70 MB RAM; MetaManager caches pod/ConfigMap/Secret metadata in local SQLite so edge nodes keep running + restart pods while cloud link is down (no rescheduling); EventBus = MQTT client to local mosquitto, DeviceTwin syncs device state, ServiceBus = REST; CloudHub (websocket) + EdgeController + DeviceController on cloud side. ONDC protocol: Beckn-based async API pairs search/on_search, select/on_select, init/on_init, confirm/on_confirm, status/on_status, track/on_track, cancel/on_cancel, update/on_update, rating, support; every request/callback signed: Authorization: Signature keyId="{subscriber_id}|{unique_key_id}|ed25519", algorithm="ed25519", created, expires, headers="(created) (expires) digest", signature=base64(Ed25519("(created): ts\n(expires): ts\ndigest: BLAKE-512=<b64 blake2b-512 of body>")); X-Gateway-Authorization added by gateway; public keys via registry /subscribe and /lookup (subscriber_id, domain, type, city); seller app must expose catalog (items, add-ons, offers, fulfilment radius/charges, payment policy) and real-time stock/price updates. Seller-side node types: Retail Aggregator or Retail Software Vendor (POS vendors like GoFrugal/Zoho act as seller apps for many stores). Reference architecture synthesis from the above (edge store node -> cloud): (1) Edge: containerised services on RPi5/Jetson under balena or Greengrass; SQLite WAL + synchronous=FULL as local source of truth; transactional outbox table; local MQTT broker (mosquitto/EMQX) with persistent sessions; camera/shelf/queue inference local; (2) Uplink: MQTT QoS1 over 4G/FWA with client-side disk queue + Message Expiry for telemetry, Greengrass Stream Manager (File persistence, OverwriteOldestData for video metrics, RejectNewData/priority for sales) or edgeHub TTL raised from 7,200 s to days; (3) Cloud: Kafka/Kinesis -> idempotent consumers (event_id dedup) -> Postgres + TimescaleDB; CRDT/LWW for catalog sync, event-sourced stock ledger; (4) Fleet: Greengrass IoT Jobs or balena releases with canary -> 10% -> 50% -> 100%, abort at 5% failure over >=100 devices, ROLLBACK policy, A/B partitions; (5) Monitoring: per-store exporters remote_write to Mimir, Alertmanager absence/heartbeat alerts, because cloud-side device status can read healthy while offline; (6) Integrations: Tally XML on port 9000 over LAN/cloud-Tally, Zoho Inventory adjustments API (<=100 req/min), SAP B1 Service Layer OData, GoFrugal/ONDC via seller-app vendor, ONDC direct via Ed25519-signed Beckn callbacks.
